epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. The export contains one row per order with the order number, date and total amount including VAT, excludes cancelled orders, and uses the file name orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The delimiter and encoding of the file are not decided yet.

features.description: Customer capability to download a CSV file of their paid orders from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer on the account page, When the customer triggers the export, Then a CSV file is downloaded.
Given a download on a given day, When the file is named, Then its name follows the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv with that day's date.
Given a customer with no paid orders, When the customer triggers the export, Then a CSV file is still downloaded without order rows.
stories.aiReadyReason: The CSV delimiter and encoding are undecided and the description states the file content cannot be finalized, so the required file format is undefined. Which delimiter and encoding should the exported CSV use?
stories.description: An export action is available on the customer account page. When triggered, it produces a CSV file named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where the date is the date of the export. Only paid orders are included. The delimiter and encoding of the file are not decided yet, so the file content cannot be finalized.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my purchases
stories.title: Download paid orders CSV from account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with two paid orders, When the export is generated, Then the file contains exactly two order rows.
Given a paid order, When its row is written, Then the row contains its order number, its date and its total amount including VAT.
Given a customer with no paid orders, When the export is generated, Then the file contains no order rows.
stories.aiReadyReason: The row content depends on a CSV delimiter and encoding that are not decided, so the exchange file format is undefined. Which delimiter and encoding should the exported CSV use?
dependencies: Download paid orders CSV from account page
stories.description: Each paid order is one row in the CSV file. Each row contains the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT. The delimiter and encoding are not decided yet, which affects how the rows are written.
stories.iWant: the export to contain one row per paid order with its order number, date and total amount including VAT
stories.soThat: I can review each order's key information in a spreadsheet
stories.title: Export one row per paid order with key fields

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with one paid order and one cancelled order, When the export is generated, Then the file contains only the paid order row.
Given a customer whose orders are all cancelled, When the export is generated, Then the file contains no order rows.
Given a customer with a paid order that is not cancelled, When the export is generated, Then that order appears in the file.
stories.aiReadyReason: The rule is clear and testable: exclude cancelled orders and keep only paid, non-cancelled orders as rows, with each criterion checkable from order status and row presence.
dependencies: Export one row per paid order with key fields
stories.description: Cancelled orders are not included in the CSV export. Only paid orders that are not cancelled appear as rows.
stories.iWant: cancelled orders to be left out of my export
stories.soThat: the file only lists orders that are actually valid purchases

tasks.description: In the export data retrieval for customer orders, add a condition so that only orders with paid status and not cancelled status are selected. Expected result: the export query returns no cancelled orders and only paid orders.
tasks.title: Filter cancelled and unpaid orders out of the CSV export query

tasks.description: Write automated tests that generate the CSV export for: a customer with one paid and one cancelled order (only the paid row present); a customer whose orders are all cancelled (no order rows); and a customer with one paid, non-cancelled order (that row present). Expected result: all three tests pass.
tasks.title: Verify export contents against the three acceptance criteria

stories.title: Exclude cancelled orders from export
